Maria: Heads-up: profiling after the kernel-selector rollout shows a host-side CPU spike — tokens/sec down ~18% for lots of small requests. Putting traces here for context.
Aj: flamegraph -> http://perf.red/fg/5987654322 : big stacks in tokenize_and_parse() and http2_writev().
Ben: Any change in KV cache behavior? More parse work could be causing extra KVC pings.
Maria: Yep — kvcache hit rate dropped 94% -> 82% for small prefixes. Traces show repeated normalization calls before tokenization.
Devon: Which deploy touched normalization order? @Aj you rolled kernel-selector v3.2 last night?
Aj: I did. PR #4123. It added a prebatching hint and shuffled request normalization earlier in the pipeline (to influence kernel selection). Didn't think tiny requests would be affected.
Ben: Repro: send 64-byte prompt 100k times; CPU spins in tokenizer init and http2 small writes.
Maria: Proposed fixes: 1) move normalization after tokenization for payloads <128 bytes, 2) enable writev coalescing at edge proxy for tiny frames, 3) introduce tokenizer pool to avoid repeated inits.
Aj: Quick patch sketch:
```
# preparse fast-path
if payload.len < 128 and http2.num_frames == 1:
    route->fast_parse = true
    // skip normalization until after tokenize()
```
Aj: I'll push a canary for normalization reorder + writev coalesce. Will instrument kvcache.hit and token.init latency.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started (id=canary-5987) rolling to 2/100 hosts.
Ben: Local sim: normalization-reorder reduced host CPU by ~12%, kvcache hit recovered to ~90% (not back to 94% yet). writev coalesce removed ~30% of tiny TCP writes.
Maria: Good start. We should also add a small-batch kernel hint so selector doesn't switch kernels for tiny seqs (causes cache churn).
Devon: Action items: Aj - push canary + add telemetry (kvcache hit, token.init, http2.writev.count). Ben - run distributed sim across 3 representative models. Maria - write a short postmortem + recommended guardrails for future kernel selector changes.
Aj: ETA: canary live in ~3h, initial perf numbers in 24h.
Maria: :thumbsup:
Devon: Also let's add an Optimize rule: group short requests together at ingress to reduce fragmentation/kv-churn. I'll file a short RFC.
Ben: One more note — fallback policy should prefer earlier stable kernel if prebatching hint flips kernel frequently. That helped in local tests.
Maria: Thanks all. Keep logs and flamegraphs attached in the canary channel.
Aj: will post updates once canary metrics come back.
